source.section: Schedule SB (PDF page 1) and its Instructions: line 4 (SB Instructions PDF page 2); line 16 and its Caution (SB Instructions PDF page 7; Publication 126 PDF page 8 section 4.E(1); Publication 106 PDF page 4 section 3.C(1)); Form 1 lines 1-12 (Form 1 PDF page 1); Form 1 Instructions PDF page 15 line 8 and lines 10a-10b (PDF pages 15-16), PDF pages 35-37 2025 Standard Deduction Table (row named in worked), PDF page 15 line 12 with the PDF pages 38-43 Tax Table and PDF page 44 Tax Computation Worksheet; tax figured from the 2025 Tax Rate Schedules, Publication 106 PDF pages 6-7

worked: Married filing jointly, both 67 or older (70 and 68): you Wisconsin Retirement System pension 20,000 (a section 414(d) government plan, counted as settled), spouse IRA 15,000, interest 40,000, Social Security 26,000 and 14,000. Qualifying income 35,000, under the 48,000 joint cap: line 16 is 35,000. Federal (given, not tested): federal AGI = ira distribution (spouse) 15,000.00 + public pension paid by WI (you) 20,000.00 + interest 40,000.00 + taxable Social Security 34,000.00 (gross 40,000.00; provisional income 75,000.00 + half of 40,000.00 = 95,000.00; taxable Social Security 34,000.00) = 109,000.00. Federal taxable income = 109,000.00 - standard deduction 31,500.00 + 2 x 1,600.00 = 74,300.00; the federal senior deduction is ignored. Form 1 line 1 federal AGI 109,000.00; line 2 Schedule I adjustments 0.00; line 3 109,000.00; line 4 additions 0.00; line 5 109,000.00. Schedule SB: line 4 Social Security adjustment = 34,000.00; line 16 retirement income subtraction: qualifying income you (age 70): pension 20,000.00 = 20,000.00; spouse (age 68): IRA 15,000.00 = 15,000.00; smaller of 35,000.00 and the 48,000.00 cap = 35,000.00; line 50 total 69,000.00. Schedule SB line 17: federal AGI 109,000.00 is not less than 30,000.00, so no 5,000 subtraction. Form 1 line 6 69,000.00; line 7 Wisconsin income = 109,000.00 - 69,000.00 = 40,000.00. Line 8 standard deduction, 2025 Standard Deduction Table (Form 1 Instructions PDF page 35), row 40,000 to less than 40,500, column Married filing jointly: 22,729.00 (printed row, at least / less than / single / joint / separate / head of household: 40,000 / 40,500 / 11,076 / 22,729 / 6,618 / 12,859). Line 9 = 40,000.00 - 22,729.00 = 17,271.00. Line 10a 2 x 700 = 1,400.00; line 10b 2 x 250 = 500.00; line 10c 1,900.00. Line 11 taxable income = 17,271.00 - 1,900.00 = 15,371.00. Line 12 tax, Schedule B (joint) as numbers: 3.5% x 15,371.00 = 537.985; total 537.985, rounded once to 537.99. The Tax Table row 15,300 to 15,400 (PDF page 39) gives 537; expected keeps the schedule. Credits (lines 13-20, 30-35): none modelled; 0.00. State income tax 537.99.
accepted_approximations: The projection always takes the 24,000/48,000 subtraction for a person 67 or older, never the Wisconsin credits it bars (see not_modelled); a household whose credits are worth more would skip it.
